title: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction
abstract: arXiv:2607.12161v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Token-reduction tools for coding agents are often evaluated by the number of tokens they remove, but token count alone does not determine end-to-end inference cost. We evaluate three token-reduction approaches against an unmodified Claude Code baseline across controlled coding tasks, measuring provider-billed cost, task success, cache traffic, and agent behavior. The largest compression setup reduced delivered tool-output tokens by 38.4% but increased billed cost by 6.8%, while lighter compression produced only small and statistically uncertain savings. Across tasks, token reduction was weakly correlated with cost reduction (Pearson r = 0.15). Cost decomposition shows that prompt-cache creation and reads dominate the measured input-side cost, leaving only a limited fraction of total spend directly addressable by tool-output compression. We also find that compression can alter agent trajectories through additional retrieval, diagnosis

translated_title: 令牌减少并非成本降低
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.12161v5 公告类型：替换 摘要：编码代理的令牌减少工具通常通过其移除的令牌数量来评估，但仅凭令牌数量并不能决定端到端的推理成本。我们在受控编码任务中，针对未修改的Claude Code基线评估了三种令牌减少方法，测量了提供商计费成本、任务成功率、缓存流量和代理行为。最大的压缩设置将交付的工具输出令牌减少了38.4%，但计费成本却增加了6.8%，而较轻的压缩仅产生了微小且统计上不确定的节省。在各种任务中，令牌减少与成本降低的相关性较弱（Pearson r = 0.15）。成本分解显示，提示缓存的创建和读取主导了测量到的输入侧成本，使得总支出中只有有限部分可直接通过工具输出压缩来解决。我们还发现，压缩可能通过额外的检索和诊断改变代理的轨迹。
tldr: 本文发现令牌减少并不等同于成本降低，因为缓存开销主导了推理成本，令牌压缩甚至可能增加实际计费成本。
en_tdlr: This paper finds that token reduction does not equate to cost reduction, as cache overhead dominates inference costs and token compression can even increase actual billed costs.
